notes: HE 0437-5439: included as follow_up because the paper treats it as the previously identified hypervelocity star (Table 1 and Edelmann et al. 2005; T:p2-b0, T:p6-b8) and analyzes its possible rejuvenated binary origin (T:p6-b2). The paper uses the established HVS classification rather than making a new present-day bound/unbound determination. US 708: included as follow_up because the paper calls it a hypervelocity star and discusses a prior binary-merger suggestion (Hirsch et al. 2005) plus a possible triple-disruption origin (T:p9-b3); it gives no new explicit bound/unbound determination.

HE 0437-5439: T:p6-b8 reports 723 km/s as HE 0437-5439's high velocity, attributed to Edelmann et al. (2005); this is the only target-specific quantity of the requested types reported in the supplied material. No equatorial coordinates, parallax, distance, proper motions, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability for this star is reported.

US 708: The paper mentions US 708 only qualitatively: it identifies it as a hypervelocity star that is an evolved sdO star and suggests it may have formed from a merger of a close binary (T:p6-b8, T:p9-b2, T:p9-b3). It reports no numerical position, distance, parallax, proper motion, radial velocity, Galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame velocity, or bound/unbound probability for US 708. The general HVS velocity threshold is a sample definition, not an individual result.
